title: GPU-less, Trust-less, Limit-less: Reimagining the Confidential AI Cloud - Mike Bursell
talk_summary: A vendor pitch for Super Protocol, a confidential-computing cloud using hardware TEEs (Intel TDX, AMD SEV, Nvidia GPU TEEs) plus blockchain smart contracts to run AI workloads on sensitive data with cryptographic attestation. The actionable content is limited to general patterns: attestation of what code ran, hash-pinned inputs, and per-job integrity reports.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before a job runs, a trusted loader inside the TEE hashes the engine image, input datasets, and config, compares them to an approved list, and blocks the job if anything diverges; an integrity report is published afterward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: calculates hashes for the engine data sets and config, compares them with the approved list, blocks the job if anything diverges

takeaways.what_they_do: A confidential VM is launched once and handles multiple jobs instead of spinning up a fresh VM per task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a confidential virtual machine or CVM is launched once and then handles multiple jobs. No need to spin up a new VM for every task

takeaways.technique: Per-job execution report as audit artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Every job emits a report listing certificates, processed inputs, hashes, and timing, retrievable by order ID and verifiable by any participant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This report shows exactly what ran, where it ran, and that it followed the expected logic.
